title: Skill Following: Evaluating Actual Skill Use in Retrieval-Enabled LLM Agents

visual_explainer.question: When an agent invokes retrieval, does the retrieved skill improve that same task rather than merely select an easier task subset?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Aggregate retrieved-vs-skipped lift can reverse sign under same-task paired evaluation, so invocation selection and realized retrieval utility must be measured separately.
visual_explainer.compared_with: aggregate retrieved-vs-skipped lift and the all-task Overall Skill-Access Effect under the same skill-enabled/skill-disabled protocol

analysis.tldr: Skill Following separates selective retrieval coverage from same-task realized utility: a model can look strong when retrieved tasks are compared with skipped tasks yet become worse when the same retrieval-invoked tasks are paired against skill-disabled execution.
analysis.problem: Autonomous retrieval jointly decides which tasks invoke a tool and what evidence reaches the model, so aggregate retrieved-versus-skipped comparisons confound call selection with the downstream value of retrieved content.
analysis.core_idea: Report an Overall Skill-Access Effect over paired tasks and a Retrieval-conditional Actual-use Effect that pairs skill-enabled versus skill-disabled outcomes on the subset where the skill-enabled run actually invoked retrieval.
analysis.agent_loop: For each task, the skill-enabled agent may call search_skills, BM25 returns top-3 procedural skills whose full text is appended, and the agent answers; the paired skill-disabled run removes search_skills while matching task, model, decoding, and seed.
analysis.retrieval_design: Small fixed coding or math skill pools are indexed with BM25 over skill descriptions and bodies; top-3 full skill texts are returned, with at most three retrieval calls per task.
compared_to: aggregate retrieved-versus-skipped lift inside skill-enabled runs
Overall Skill-Access Effect over all paired tasks
schema-empty, filler, random-skill, and corrupted-skill controls
analysis.evidence: For Gemini-2.5-Flash-lite, aggregate lift versus RAE is +6.2/-15.6, +16.2/-15.9, and +4.4/-22.2 across three MBPP+ partitions; HumanEval+ is -0.1/-21.1. The sign reversal shows that selective invocation can dominate the conventional aggregate story.
analysis.why_it_matters: Retrieval evaluation needs to separate whether an agent chooses to acquire evidence from whether the acquired evidence improves the same task after it enters the trajectory.
limitations: RAE conditions on the skill-enabled run’s own post-treatment retrieval subset, so it is a protocol-conditional paired signal rather than an unbiased causal effect over a pre-treatment population.
Skill-enabled and skill-disabled runs differ in tool availability, and heterogeneous filler/random/corrupted controls do not isolate one content-use mechanism.
The study uses small fixed procedural-skill pools and single-pass coding/math tasks, while complete token, tool, latency, and dollar accounting is not reported.
